title: Final: which format do you need
sub: The whole course mixed together, from STL to LAZ
cards/1/q: Match each task to a format
cards/1/pairs/1/0: Show a model on a website
cards/1/pairs/2/0: Send a part to another CAD system
cards/1/pairs/3/0: Move a BIM model between programs
cards/3/task: A scan with vertex colors: find a simple format, with no scenes or animation, that keeps the color.
cards/4/q: Which format stores exact geometry rather than triangles?
cards/4/explain: STEP holds B-rep and NURBS. The others are triangles or points.
cards/5/q: A LAS point has class 6. What is it?
cards/5/explain: 2 is ground, 5 is high vegetation, 6 is building, 9 is water.
cards/6/q: Which formats are open standards? Select all.
cards/6/explain: RVT and DWG are closed Autodesk formats.
cards/7/q: To show a STEP file in a browser, you need to…
cards/7/options/0: Tessellate it into triangles and save it as, say, GLB
cards/8/q: You got an .rcp without .rcs files and an .obj without an .mtl. What do they have in common?
cards/8/options/0: They are files of references: without the files they point to, the data is incomplete
cards/8/explain: External references are the top cause of “broken” transfers in 3D. The fix is single-file packages: GLB, USDZ, NWD, E57.
cards/9/explain: The course’s four worlds in one chain.
